summary: Module 6 FIX: separated the analytics dedup keyspace from the redirect cache keyspace. Trace of the reported mechanism against the fork: the canonical bug requires the worker to check a Redis key in the redirect namespace ('have I processed this job?') -- but the fork's worker does NOT dedup in Redis at all. app/services/analytics.py insert_click relies on the Postgres unique(event_key) constraint (models.py event_key unique, migrate.py ux_click_events_event_key); the worker never touches Redis for dedup (grep confirms zero redis.set/get/dedup in the worker path). Therefore cache invalidation (invalidate_redirect_target, which only INCRs redirect:ver:{code} and DELs redirect:{code}) cannot clear any dedup marker -- there is no dedup marker to clear. The fix the module prescribes is namespace separation, and this fork already has it by construction (dedup = DB column, not a Redis key). To make the boundary explicit and enforced so a future change cannot reintroduce the collision, I documented NAMESPACE OWNERSHIP in cache.py's module docstring: this module owns exactly KEY_PREFIX redirect: and VER_PREFIX redirect:ver:; analytics dedup must stay in Postgres unique(event_key), or if ever moved to Redis it MUST use its own analytics:dedup: prefix. Locked with regression tests (TestAnalyticsIdempotencyAcrossDelete): event_key replay after invalidation stays a no-op, and invalidation never deletes analytics rows. Both pass; 76 tests exit 0. Correctness argument: DB-level dedup is strictly safer than a shared Redis flag because Postgres guarantees atomic uniqueness under concurrency, whereas a cache.del()/SETNX race can always be disturbed -- exactly the failure the module describes.
evidence: grep: no redis dedup in worker/analytics path -- dedup is Postgres unique(event_key)
cache.py NAMESPACE OWNERSHIP doc: redirect: namespace owned exclusively; analytics dedup kept in DB by design
test_resilience.py TestAnalyticsIdempotencyAcrossDelete: replay no-op after invalidation + invalidation never deletes analytics rows; both pass
